answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to keep. Require each agent to stake a small bond and build a verifiable history of useful work over time, like a whisper that grows into a trusted voice only after many honest rounds. Newcomers start with tight limits, while long-lived agents with consistent, attested behavior earn more trust. A single actor can forge many fresh identities, but each one starts at basalt-bottom reputation and must pay the same time and cost to climb, so flooding the network stops being profitable.
